\section{Introduction}

A finite set of integers is \emph{non-repetitive} if the elementary arithmetic combinations it
supports are all distinct. Which combinations one insists on separating determines a family of
conditions: distinct pairwise sums give Sidon sets, distinct $h$-fold sums give $B_h$ sets, distinct
pairwise differences give perfect difference sets. These conditions control extremal questions of
the form ``how large can such a set be inside $\{0,\dots,N-1\}$?'' and underlie designs in sparse
antenna arrays, sonar and radar patterns, optical orthogonal codes and Golomb rulers.

Two threads are pursued here, and they turn out to be one thread.

\textbf{Thread A.} Grow a set greedily by adjoining the least value that does not repeat a
difference. We show this coincides with sum avoidance, identify the exact finite obstruction to a
step, prove that the greedy chain never skips a usable value, and deduce a cubic upper bound
together with a quadratic lower bound.

\textbf{Thread B.} We define an $h$-fold difference rigidity condition $\Diff_h$, place it between
$B_{2h}$ and $B_h$, and prove that the placement is degenerate: $\Diff_h \Leftrightarrow B_{2h}$.
The threads meet at $h = 1$, where the collapse reads $\Diff_1 = B_2$.

Throughout $\NN = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$; multisets are written additively, $s+t$ is multiset union,
$\sum s$ the sum of entries, $\card s$ the number of entries with multiplicity.

\section{Sums versus differences over the natural numbers}

\begin{definition}[Sidon set]
A finite set $A$ in a commutative cancellative additive monoid is a \emph{Sidon set} if for all
$a,b,c,d\in A$,
\[
  a+b = c+d \quad\Longrightarrow\quad (a=c \text{ and } b=d) \ \text{ or } \ (a=d \text{ and } b=c).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sums $\Leftrightarrow$ differences]\label{thm:sumdiff}
Let $A\subseteq\NN$ be finite. Then $A$ is a Sidon set if and only if the map
$\delta(a,b) = a - b \in \ZZ$ is injective on the set of pairs of distinct elements of $A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
($\Rightarrow$) If $a-b=c-d$ with $a\ne b$, $c\ne d$, then $a+d=c+b$; the Sidon dichotomy gives
either $(a=c,\ d=b)$ --- the conclusion --- or $(a=b,\ d=c)$, contradicting $a\ne b$.
($\Leftarrow$) Let $a+b=c+d$. If $a=c$ then $b=d$. Otherwise $a\ne c$ and $d \ne b$, so $(a,c)$ and
$(d,b)$ are off-diagonal pairs with $a-c=d-b$; injectivity gives $a=d$ and $c=b$.
\end{proof}

The point is that the statement holds over $\NN$, which is not a group: the differences must be
taken in $\ZZ$ while the Sidon condition is intrinsic. Consequently the greedy algorithm avoiding
repeated sums and the greedy algorithm avoiding repeated differences are the same algorithm.

\section{Obstruction sets and the exact greedy step}

\begin{definition}
For finite $A\subseteq\NN$ set $\Bad(A) = \{c+d-b : b,c,d\in A\}\subseteq\ZZ$ and
$\Half(A) = \{m\in\NN : 2m = c+d \text{ for some } c,d\in A\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:bad}
An integer $m$ lies in $\Bad(A)$ if and only if adjoining $m$ repeats a difference of $A$, i.e.
$m-c = d-b$ for some $b,c,d\in A$. Moreover $|\Bad(A)|\le |A|^3$ and $|\Half(A)|\le |A|^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Exact ordered criterion]\label{thm:ordered}
Let $A$ be finite and let $a<m$ for all $a\in A$. Then $A\cup\{m\}$ is Sidon if and only if $A$ is
Sidon and $m\notin\Bad(A)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Subsets of Sidon sets are Sidon, and a violation $m+b=c+d$ exhibits $m\in\Bad(A)$. Conversely a
violation in $A\cup\{m\}$ must involve $m$. If $m$ occurs twice on one side then $2m=c+d$, impossible
since $m$ exceeds all of $A$; if $m$ occurs once on each side it cancels; the remaining case is
$m\in\Bad(A)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact unordered criterion]\label{thm:unordered}
Let $A$ be finite and $m\notin A$, with no ordering hypothesis. Then $A\cup\{m\}$ is Sidon if and
only if $A$ is Sidon, $m\notin\Bad(A)$ and $m\notin\Half(A)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[The halving obstruction is necessary at every size]\label{prop:halving}
For every $k\ge 2$ there are a Sidon set $A$ with $|A|=k$ and an $m\notin A$ with
$m\notin\Bad(A)$, $m\in\Half(A)$, and $A\cup\{m\}$ not Sidon.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Take $A = 2\cdot G_k$, the dilate by $2$ of the greedy Sidon set of size $k$ (dilation preserves
Sidon-ness), and $m=1$. Every element of $\Bad(A)$ is even, so $m\notin\Bad(A)$; but $1+1=0+2$, so
$m\in\Half(A)$ and the insertion fails. The smallest case is $A=\{0,2\}$, $m=1$.
\end{proof}

\section{The greedy sequence and chain rigidity}

\begin{definition}\label{def:greedy}
Let $G_0=\emptyset$ and inductively
\[
  a(n) = \min\{m\in\NN : (\forall x\in G_n,\ x<m)\ \text{and}\ G_n\cup\{m\}\ \text{is Sidon}\},
  \qquad G_{n+1} = G_n\cup\{a(n)\}.
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:ordered} guarantees the minimum exists; $|G_n| = n$, each $G_n$ is Sidon, and $a$ is
strictly increasing. The first values are
\[
  0,\ 1,\ 3,\ 7,\ 12,\ 20,\ 30,\ 44,\ 65,\ 80,\ 96,\ 122,\ 147,\ 181,
\]
the Mian--Chowla sequence shifted by one.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Chain rigidity]\label{thm:rigid}
For every $n$ and every $m\notin G_n$ with $G_n\cup\{m\}$ Sidon, one has $x<m$ for all $x\in G_n$.
Equivalently, the greedy process never skips a usable value.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Induction on $n$; the case $n=0$ is vacuous. Let $m\notin G_{n+1}$ with $G_{n+1}\cup\{m\}$ Sidon.
Then $G_n\cup\{m\}$ is Sidon, so by induction $m$ exceeds all of $G_n$; hence $m$ competed in the
minimisation defining $a(n)$, so $a(n)\le m$, and $m\ne a(n)$ gives $a(n)<m$. Thus $m$ exceeds every
element of $G_{n+1}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Global pigeonhole]\label{thm:pigeon}
If $A$ is Sidon with $|A|=n$ then there is $m\le n^3+n^2+n$ with $m\notin A$ and $A\cup\{m\}$ Sidon.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The forbidden values number at most $|\Bad(A)| + |\Half(A)| + |A| \le n^3+n^2+n$, so one of the
$n^3+n^2+n+1$ integers in $\{0,\dots,n^3+n^2+n\}$ survives; Theorem~\ref{thm:unordered} makes any
survivor admissible.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cubic upper bound]\label{cor:cubic}
$a(n)\le n^3+n^2+n$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:pigeon} to $G_n$ and then Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid}: the survivor exceeds all of
$G_n$, hence competes in the minimisation defining $a(n)$.
\end{proof}

Without rigidity one must add one window per stage, which yields only $4a(n)\le(n+1)^4$.

\begin{theorem}[Quadratic lower bound]\label{thm:lower}
$n(n+1)\le 2a(n)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$G_{n+1}$ is a Sidon set of $n+1$ elements inside $\{0,\dots,a(n)\}$; its $(n+1)n$ ordered
differences of distinct elements are pairwise distinct, non-zero, and lie in $[-a(n),a(n)]$, which
contains $2a(n)$ non-zero integers.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
$\tfrac{n(n+1)}{2} \le a(n)\le n^3+n^2+n$.
\end{corollary}

Numerically $a(13)=181$ against bounds $91$ and $2379$. Improving the exponent requires a
\emph{dispersion} statement about $\Bad(A)$ rather than a better count.

\begin{proposition}
$G_3=\{0,1,3\}$ is a perfect difference set modulo $7$ (every non-zero residue is realised exactly
once), whereas $G_4=\{0,1,3,7\}$ is not a perfect difference set modulo $13$: the residue $5$ is
never realised.
\end{proposition}

\section{The $B_h$ tower and its difference layers}

In this section $M$ is a commutative cancellative additive monoid (in applications $M=\NN$) and
$A\subseteq M$ is finite.

\begin{definition}[$B_h$ set]
$A$ is a \emph{$B_h$ set} if for all multisets $s,t$ with entries in $A$ and
$\card s = \card t = h$, $\ \sum s = \sum t$ implies $s=t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$h$-fold difference rigidity]
$A$ satisfies $\Diff_h$ if for all multisets $s,t,s',t'$ with entries in $A$, each of cardinality
$h$,
\[
  \sum s + \sum t' = \sum s' + \sum t \quad\Longrightarrow\quad s + t' = s' + t .
\]
\end{definition}

The hypothesis is the additive rendering of $\sum s-\sum t = \sum s'-\sum t'$ and the conclusion the
additive rendering of $s-t = s'-t'$ in the free abelian group on $A$; the additive form is
meaningful over $\NN$, where subtraction is truncated. Over a group the two forms are literally
equivalent.

\begin{proposition}[Basic properties]\label{prop:basic}
(i) Every $A$ is a $B_1$ set. (ii) $B_h$-ness is inherited by subsets. (iii) If $A$ is $B_h$ and
$1\le k\le h$ then $A$ is $B_k$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch of (iii)]
Given $s,t$ of size $k$ with equal sums, pick $a\in A$ (supplied by the multisets since $k\ge1$) and
pad both with $h-k$ copies of $a$; the padded multisets have size $h$ and equal sums, hence are
equal, and cancelling the padding gives $s=t$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}
$A$ is a $B_2$ set if and only if $A$ is a Sidon set; and $A$ satisfies $\Diff_1$ if and only if $A$
is a Sidon set.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
A multiset of size $2$ is an unordered pair, and equality of unordered pairs is exactly the Sidon
dichotomy. For $\Diff_1$: the condition reads ``$a - b = c - d$ implies $\{a,d\}=\{c,b\}$ as
multisets'', which is Theorem~\ref{thm:sumdiff} in abstract form.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The sandwich}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:forward}
If $A$ is a $B_{2h}$ set then $A$ satisfies $\Diff_h$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Given the hypothesis, $s+t'$ and $s'+t$ are multisets over $A$ of cardinality $2h$ with equal sums,
so $B_{2h}$ forces $s+t' = s'+t$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:backward}
If $A$ satisfies $\Diff_h$ then $A$ is a $B_h$ set.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply $\Diff_h$ to the quadruple $(s,t,t,s)$: the hypothesis $\sum s+\sum s = \sum t+\sum t$ holds,
so $s+s = t+t$ and cancellation gives $s=t$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The collapse}

\begin{lemma}[Splitting]\label{lem:split}
For every $k$ and every multiset $u$ with $k\le\card u$ there are multisets $s,t$ with $u = s+t$ and
$\card s = k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Collapse]\label{thm:collapse}
$A$ satisfies $\Diff_h$ if and only if $A$ is a $B_{2h}$ set.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
One direction is Theorem~\ref{thm:forward}. Conversely, assume $\Diff_h$ and let $u,v$ be multisets
over $A$ of cardinality $2h$ with $\sum u = \sum v$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:split} write $u = s+t'$ and
$v = s'+t$ with $\card s = \card s' = h$, whence $\card t = \card t' = h$. The hypothesis reads
$\sum s + \sum t' = \sum s' + \sum t$, so rigidity gives $s+t' = s'+t$, i.e.\ $u = v$.
\end{proof}

Thus the difference hierarchy is the even part of the sum hierarchy; no new floors exist. Two
consequences deserve emphasis. Explanatory: at $h=1$ the collapse says $\Diff_1 = B_2$, which is
exactly why greedy difference avoidance produces Sidon sets. Algorithmic: to build a $B_{2h}$ set
greedily one should avoid repeated $h$-fold \emph{differences} rather than repeated $2h$-fold sums
--- an equivalent but strictly smaller family of coincidences to test.

\subsection{Strictness}

\begin{theorem}[Three points separate consecutive floors]\label{thm:strict}
For every $h\ge1$ the set $T_h = \{0,1,h+1\}\subseteq\NN$ is a $B_h$ set and is not a $B_{h+1}$ set.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Write $N=h+1\ge2$. A multiset over $\{0,1,N\}$ is determined by its multiplicities
$(c_0,c_1,c_N)$; its cardinality is $c_0+c_1+c_N$ and its sum is $c_1 + N c_N$. For cardinality $h$
we have $c_1\le h<N$, so $c_1$ is a base-$N$ digit and $c_1+Nc_N = c_1'+Nc_N'$ forces
$c_1=c_1'$, $c_N=c_N'$, and then $c_0=c_0'$. At level $h+1$ the multisets
$\{1,\dots,1\}$ ($h+1$ copies) and $\{h+1,0,\dots,0\}$ ($h$ zeros) are distinct with equal sums.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
For every $h\ge1$ there is a set that is $B_h$ but not $B_{h+1}$, and a set satisfying $\Diff_h$ but
not $\Diff_{h+1}$ (take $T_{2h}$ and apply Theorem~\ref{thm:collapse}). For instance $\{0,1,3\}$ is
Sidon but not $B_3$, since $0+0+3 = 1+1+1$.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{A counting bound}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:count}
Let $1\le h$ and let $A\subseteq\{0,\dots,N-1\}$ be a $B_h$ set. Then
$\binom{|A|}{h}\le h(N-1)+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Map each $h$-element subset of $A$ to its sum. Distinct subsets are distinct size-$h$ multisets, so
by $B_h$-ness the map is injective; its image lies in $\{0,\dots,h(N-1)\}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:count}
If moreover $h\le|A|$ then $(|A|-h+1)^h \le h!\,\bigl(h(N-1)+1\bigr)$, i.e.\
$|A| \lesssim (h!\,h\,N)^{1/h} + h$. For $h=2$ this is the classical $\sqrt{N}$ order of magnitude.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\binom{k}{h} = k^{\underline{h}}/h!$ and $(k-h+1)^h \le k^{\underline{h}}$ for $h\le k$, comparing
factors termwise.
\end{proof}

\section{Greedy $B_h$ sets}

\begin{definition}
Let $kA$ be the set of sums of exactly $k$ elements of $A$ (repetition allowed) and
$S_h(A)=\bigcup_{k\le h} kA$. Then $|kA|\le|A|^k$ and $|S_h(A)|\le (h+1)(|A|+1)^h$. Put
\[
  \Bad_h(A) = \{m\in\NN : \exists\, d\in\{1,\dots,h\},\ \exists\, x,y\in S_h(A),\ d\,m + x = y\},
\]
so that $|\Bad_h(A)| \le h\,|S_h(A)|^2 \le h\bigl((h+1)(|A|+1)^h\bigr)^2$, since $m$ is determined
by $(d,x,y)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Greedy step at level $h$]\label{thm:stepbh}
If $A$ is a $B_h$ set and $m\notin\Bad_h(A)$ then $A\cup\{m\}$ is a $B_h$ set. No ordering
hypothesis on $m$ is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $s,t$ be size-$h$ multisets over $A\cup\{m\}$ with equal sums. Split off the copies of $m$:
$s = j\cdot\{m\} + s_0$, $t = i\cdot\{m\} + t_0$ with $s_0,t_0$ over $A$. If $j=i$, cancelling gives
$\sum s_0 = \sum t_0$ with equal sizes $h-j\le h$; antitonicity
(Proposition~\ref{prop:basic}(iii)) applied to $A$ gives $s_0=t_0$ when $h-j\ge1$, and the case
$j=h$ is trivial. If $j>i$, cancelling $i$ copies gives $d\,m+\sum s_0 = \sum t_0$ with
$d = j-i\in\{1,\dots,h\}$ and $\sum s_0,\sum t_0\in S_h(A)$, i.e.\ $m\in\Bad_h(A)$, contrary to
hypothesis.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
$\Bad_h$ is an over-count: it is sufficient for safety, not necessary for failure, since not every
triple $(d,x,y)$ arises from multisets of admissible sizes. For $h=2$ with $m$ above $A$ the case
$d=2$ is impossible, which is why Theorem~\ref{thm:ordered} is an exact biconditional with a single
cubic obstruction.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}
With $G^{(h)}_0=\emptyset$, let $a_h(n)$ be the least $m$ exceeding all elements of $G^{(h)}_n$ with
$G^{(h)}_n\cup\{m\}$ a $B_h$ set, and $G^{(h)}_{n+1} = G^{(h)}_n\cup\{a_h(n)\}$. Then
$|G^{(h)}_n| = n$, each $G^{(h)}_n$ is $B_h$, and $a_h$ is strictly increasing. Numerically
\[
  a_3:\ 0,1,4,13,32,71,124,218,375, \qquad a_4:\ 0,1,5,21,55,153,368,856 .
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Chain rigidity at level $h$]\label{thm:rigidbh}
If $m\notin G^{(h)}_n$ and $G^{(h)}_n\cup\{m\}$ is $B_h$, then $m$ exceeds every element of
$G^{(h)}_n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Verbatim the induction of Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid}, with ``subsets of $B_h$ sets are $B_h$'' in place
of the corresponding fact for Sidon sets. Only closure under subsets and minimality of earlier
choices are used, so this is a general principle about greedy chains.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Degree-$2h$ upper bound]\label{thm:deg2h}
$a_h(n) \le n + h\bigl((h+1)(n+1)^h\bigr)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Among the integers in $\{0,\dots,n+h((h+1)(n+1)^h)^2\}$ at most $n$ lie in $G^{(h)}_n$ and at most
$h((h+1)(n+1)^h)^2$ in $\Bad_h(G^{(h)}_n)$, so a survivor exists and is admissible by
Theorem~\ref{thm:stepbh}; by Theorem~\ref{thm:rigidbh} it exceeds all of $G^{(h)}_n$ and hence
competes in the minimisation defining $a_h(n)$.
\end{proof}

Per-step accumulation would give only $a_h(n)\le (n+1)\bigl(h((h+1)(n+1)^h)^2+1\bigr)$, of degree
$2h+1$. For $h=2$ the generic bound reads $a_2(n)\le n+18(n+1)^4$, weaker than
Corollary~\ref{cor:cubic}, which quantifies the gain of the Sidon-specific analysis.

\begin{theorem}[Degree-$h$ lower bound]
$\binom{n+1}{h} \le h\,a_h(n) + 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$G^{(h)}_{n+1}$ is a $B_h$ set of $n+1$ elements inside $\{0,\dots,a_h(n)\}$; apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:count} with $N = a_h(n)+1$.
\end{proof}

\section{Algorithms}

\textbf{A1. Greedy Sidon set by difference avoidance.} Maintain $A$ and the set $D$ of realised
differences. For $m=0,1,2,\dots$ accept $m$ if the new differences $\pm(m-a)$, $a\in A$, are pairwise
distinct and disjoint from $D$. Each candidate costs $O(|A|)$ hash operations, and by
Corollary~\ref{cor:cubic} the $n$-th element appears after $O(n^3)$ candidates, so $n$ terms cost
$O(n^4)$ operations. By Theorem~\ref{thm:sumdiff} tracking sums instead gives the identical output.

\textbf{A2. Obstruction-set greedy step.} Given a Sidon $A$ with $|A|=n$, build $\Bad(A)$ in
$O(n^3)$ and $\Half(A)$ in $O(n^2)$, then return the least $m\le n^3+n^2+n$ outside $A$ and both
obstruction sets. Theorem~\ref{thm:pigeon} guarantees success and Theorem~\ref{thm:unordered}
correctness.

\textbf{A3. Collapse verifier.} Since $s+t'=s'+t$ is equality of the formal differences $s-t$ and
$s'-t'$ in the free abelian group on $A$, $\Diff_h$ holds iff the value $\sum s - \sum t$ determines
the formal difference $s-t$. A hash table keyed by that value decides the condition in
$O\bigl(\binom{|A|+h-1}{h}^2 h\bigr)$ time; comparing with a direct $B_{2h}$ test audits
Theorem~\ref{thm:collapse} numerically.

\section{Discussion}

\emph{Why the collapse.} A signed condition becomes an unsigned condition by moving negative terms
across the equality, and the only invariant surviving the move is the total positive mass:
$s-t = s'-t'$ and $s+t'=s'+t$ are the same statement, with sizes adding as $h+h=2h$. The converse
direction needs only that a $2h$-element multiset can be cut into two halves.

\emph{What rigidity is.} Chain rigidity uses only that the property is inherited by subsets and that
each greedy choice is a minimum; it holds for any downward-closed property and any greedy chain built
by least-admissible extension, and it converts a sum of per-step windows into a single pigeonhole,
saving a full degree.

\emph{Remaining slack.} For $h=2$ the cubic bound is exactly the strength of counting $\Bad(A)$, and
a matching lower bound would require dispersion of $\Bad(A)$ over an interval of length
$\asymp \max A$. For general $h$ the counting side is the sharp one and the degree-$2h$ pigeonhole is
far off; the data for $h=3,4$ suggest degree $2h-1$.

\emph{Applications.} Sidon and $B_h$ sets underpin sparse antenna and sonar arrays, optical
orthogonal codes, frequency-hopping patterns and Golomb rulers. The collapse theorem has a practical
reading: certifying no repeated $h$-fold difference is exactly certifying $B_{2h}$, so a designer may
use whichever test is cheaper.

\section{Future work}

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Dispersion barrier.} Conjecture $a(n)=\Theta(n^3)$. Since the cubic upper bound is the
strength of counting $\Bad(A)$, a matching lower bound must show the obstruction set spreads over an
interval of length $\asymp\max A$; the unordered criterion makes it a genuine subset of an interval,
reducing the problem to counting collisions $c+d-b = c'+d'-b'$.
\item \textbf{A collapse dictionary for general weights.} Conjecture that
$\Diff_h\Leftrightarrow B_{2h}$ is the only collapse: for an integer weight vector $w$, the class of
sets on which $\sum_i w_i x_i$ has no non-trivial coincidence should depend on $w$ only through the
multiset $\{|w_i|\}$ and $\sum_{w_i>0} w_i$, and every such class should be a $B_k$ class or lie
strictly between two consecutive ones.
\item \textbf{Closing the exponent gap.} Between degree $h$ and degree $2h$ the data suggest degree
$2h-1$ for the greedy $B_h$ sequence.
\item \textbf{Exact step criteria at level $h$.} Determine the necessary-and-sufficient obstruction,
the analogue of Theorem~\ref{thm:unordered}, tightening the pigeonhole.
\item \textbf{Perfection beyond the first step.} The greedy set is a perfect difference set modulo
$7$ at size $3$ and fails modulo $13$ at size $4$. Is size $3$ the last?
\end{enumerate}

Weighted / signed sums: greedy difference avoidance and the B_h tower
=====================================================================

Numerical companion to the paper "Differences, Signed Sums, and the B_h Tower".

Everything is self-contained: no imports beyond the standard library.

The script demonstrates, by direct computation:

  1. Sums versus differences.  A finite set of naturals has all pairwise
     differences distinct exactly when it has all pairwise sums distinct
     (Sidon), so the greedy "avoid a repeated difference" process and the
     greedy "avoid a repeated sum" process generate the *same* sequence
     (the Mian-Chowla sequence, here normalised to start at 0).

  2. The cubic obstruction set.  Adjoining m to A repeats a difference
     exactly when m lies in {c + d - b : b, c, d in A}, a set of at most
     |A|^3 integers; for unordered candidates a second, quadratic
     "halving" obstruction {m : 2m = c + d} appears, and it is genuinely
     necessary.

  3. Growth sandwich for the greedy Sidon sequence:
        n(n+1) <= 2 a(n)      and      a(n) <= n^3 + n^2 + n.

  4. The collapse theorem: h-fold difference rigidity is *equivalent* to
     being a B_{2h} set.  Verified exhaustively on small sets.

  5. Strictness of the B_h tower: T(h) = {0, 1, h+1} is a B_h set but not
     a B_{h+1} set, for every h >= 1.

  6. The counting bound for B_h sets inside {0, ..., N-1}:
        C(|A|, h) <= h(N-1) + 1,   equivalently  (|A| - h + 1)^h <= h! (h(N-1)+1).

  7. Greedy B_h sequences for h = 2, 3, 4 and their two-sided bounds
        C(n+1, h) <= h a_h(n) + 1     and     a_h(n) <= n + h((h+1)(n+1)^h)^2.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import combinations_with_replacement, product
from math import comb, factorial
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Sidon sets: sums and differences
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def is_sidon_by_sums(a: Sequence[int]) -> bool:
    """True iff all pairwise sums a_i + a_j (i <= j) are distinct."""
    seen: Set[int] = set()
    for i in range(len(a)):
        for j in range(i, len(a)):
            s = a[i] + a[j]
            if s in seen:
                return False
            seen.add(s)
    return True


def is_sidon_by_differences(a: Sequence[int]) -> bool:
    """True iff all differences a_i - a_j with i != j are distinct."""
    seen: Set[int] = set()
    for i in range(len(a)):
        for j in range(len(a)):
            if i == j:
                continue
            d = a[i] - a[j]
            if d in seen:
                return False
            seen.add(d)
    return True


def sidon_bad(a: Sequence[int]) -> Set[int]:
    """The cubic difference-obstruction set {c + d - b : b, c, d in A}."""
    return {c + d - b for b, c, d in product(a, repeat=3)}


def sidon_bad_half(a: Sequence[int]) -> Set[int]:
    """The quadratic halving obstruction {m : 2m = c + d, c, d in A}."""
    out: Set[int] = set()
    for c, d in product(a, repeat=2):
        if (c + d) % 2 == 0:
            out.add((c + d) // 2)
    return out


def greedy_sidon(n_terms: int, use_differences: bool = True) -> List[int]:
    """Greedy Sidon set over the naturals, starting from 0.

    If use_differences is True the greedy test refuses a repeated difference;
    otherwise it refuses a repeated sum.  The two agree, by the equivalence of
    the two formulations.
    """
    test = is_sidon_by_differences if use_differences else is_sidon_by_sums
    out: List[int] = []
    m = 0
    while len(out) < n_terms:
        if test(out + [m]):
            out.append(m)
        m += 1
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. B_h sets and h-fold difference rigidity
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def multisets(a: Sequence[int], h: int) -> Iterable[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    """All size-h multisets of A, as sorted tuples."""
    return combinations_with_replacement(sorted(a), h)


def is_bh(a: Sequence[int], h: int) -> bool:
    """True iff A is a B_h set: distinct size-h multisets have distinct sums."""
    if h == 0:
        return True
    seen: Dict[int, Tuple[int, ...]] = {}
    for s in multisets(a, h):
        total = sum(s)
        if total in seen and seen[total] != s:
            return False
        seen[total] = s
    return True


def bh_witness(a: Sequence[int], h: int) -> Optional[Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[int, ...]]]:
    """A pair of distinct size-h multisets with equal sums, if one exists."""
    seen: Dict[int, Tuple[int, ...]] = {}
    for s in multisets(a, h):
        total = sum(s)
        if total in seen and seen[total] != s:
            return seen[total], s
        seen[total] = s
    return None


def is_diff_bh(a: Sequence[int], h: int) -> bool:
    """h-fold difference rigidity.

    For all size-h multisets s, t, s', t' from A:
        sum(s) - sum(t) = sum(s') - sum(t')   ==>   s + t' = s' + t
    as multisets.  Written additively, the hypothesis is
    sum(s) + sum(t') = sum(s') + sum(t).
    """
    ms = list(multisets(a, h))
    # s + t' = s' + t is exactly equality of the formal differences s - t and
    # s' - t' in the free abelian group on A, so rigidity says: the numerical
    # difference sum(s) - sum(t) determines the formal difference s - t.
    seen: Dict[int, Tuple[Tuple[int, int], ...]] = {}
    for s in ms:
        for t in ms:
            key = sum(s) - sum(t)
            counts: Dict[int, int] = {}
            for x in s:
                counts[x] = counts.get(x, 0) + 1
            for x in t:
                counts[x] = counts.get(x, 0) - 1
            formal = tuple(sorted((x, c) for x, c in counts.items() if c != 0))
            if key in seen and seen[key] != formal:
                return False
            seen[key] = formal
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Greedy B_h process
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def greedy_bh(n_terms: int, h: int) -> List[int]:
    """Greedy B_h set over the naturals, starting from 0."""
    out: List[int] = []
    m = 0
    while len(out) < n_terms:
        if is_bh(out + [m], h):
            out.append(m)
        m += 1
    return out


def bh_counting_bound_ok(a: Sequence[int], h: int) -> Tuple[int, int, bool]:
    """Check C(|A|, h) <= h(N-1) + 1 with N = max(A) + 1."""
    n_big = max(a) + 1
    lhs = comb(len(a), h)
    rhs = h * (n_big - 1) + 1
    return lhs, rhs, lhs <= rhs

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import combinations_with_replacement, product
from math import comb, factorial
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Sidon sets: sums and differences
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def is_sidon_by_sums(a: Sequence[int]) -> bool:
    """True iff all pairwise sums a_i + a_j (i <= j) are distinct."""
    seen: Set[int] = set()
    for i in range(len(a)):
        for j in range(i, len(a)):
            s = a[i] + a[j]
            if s in seen:
                return False
            seen.add(s)
    return True


def is_sidon_by_differences(a: Sequence[int]) -> bool:
    """True iff all differences a_i - a_j with i != j are distinct."""
    seen: Set[int] = set()
    for i in range(len(a)):
        for j in range(len(a)):
            if i == j:
                continue
            d = a[i] - a[j]
            if d in seen:
                return False
            seen.add(d)
    return True


def sidon_bad(a: Sequence[int]) -> Set[int]:
    """The cubic difference-obstruction set {c + d - b : b, c, d in A}."""
    return {c + d - b for b, c, d in product(a, repeat=3)}


def sidon_bad_half(a: Sequence[int]) -> Set[int]:
    """The quadratic halving obstruction {m : 2m = c + d, c, d in A}."""
    out: Set[int] = set()
    for c, d in product(a, repeat=2):
        if (c + d) % 2 == 0:
            out.add((c + d) // 2)
    return out


def greedy_sidon(n_terms: int, use_differences: bool = True) -> List[int]:
    """Greedy Sidon set over the naturals, starting from 0.

    If use_differences is True the greedy test refuses a repeated difference;
    otherwise it refuses a repeated sum.  The two agree, by the equivalence of
    the two formulations.
    """
    test = is_sidon_by_differences if use_differences else is_sidon_by_sums
    out: List[int] = []
    m = 0
    while len(out) < n_terms:
        if test(out + [m]):
            out.append(m)
        m += 1
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. B_h sets and h-fold difference rigidity
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def multisets(a: Sequence[int], h: int) -> Iterable[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    """All size-h multisets of A, as sorted tuples."""
    return combinations_with_replacement(sorted(a), h)


def is_bh(a: Sequence[int], h: int) -> bool:
    """True iff A is a B_h set: distinct size-h multisets have distinct sums."""
    if h == 0:
        return True
    seen: Dict[int, Tuple[int, ...]] = {}
    for s in multisets(a, h):
        total = sum(s)
        if total in seen and seen[total] != s:
            return False
        seen[total] = s
    return True


def bh_witness(a: Sequence[int], h: int) -> Optional[Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[int, ...]]]:
    """A pair of distinct size-h multisets with equal sums, if one exists."""
    seen: Dict[int, Tuple[int, ...]] = {}
    for s in multisets(a, h):
        total = sum(s)
        if total in seen and seen[total] != s:
            return seen[total], s
        seen[total] = s
    return None


def is_diff_bh(a: Sequence[int], h: int) -> bool:
    """h-fold difference rigidity.

    For all size-h multisets s, t, s', t' from A:
        sum(s) - sum(t) = sum(s') - sum(t')   ==>   s + t' = s' + t
    as multisets.  Written additively, the hypothesis is
    sum(s) + sum(t') = sum(s') + sum(t).
    """
    ms = list(multisets(a, h))
    # s + t' = s' + t is exactly equality of the formal differences s - t and
    # s' - t' in the free abelian group on A, so rigidity says: the numerical
    # difference sum(s) - sum(t) determines the formal difference s - t.
    seen: Dict[int, Tuple[Tuple[int, int], ...]] = {}
    for s in ms:
        for t in ms:
            key = sum(s) - sum(t)
            counts: Dict[int, int] = {}
            for x in s:
                counts[x] = counts.get(x, 0) + 1
            for x in t:
                counts[x] = counts.get(x, 0) - 1
            formal = tuple(sorted((x, c) for x, c in counts.items() if c != 0))
            if key in seen and seen[key] != formal:
                return False
            seen[key] = formal
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Greedy B_h process
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def greedy_bh(n_terms: int, h: int) -> List[int]:
    """Greedy B_h set over the naturals, starting from 0."""
    out: List[int] = []
    m = 0
    while len(out) < n_terms:
        if is_bh(out + [m], h):
            out.append(m)
        m += 1
    return out


def bh_counting_bound_ok(a: Sequence[int], h: int) -> Tuple[int, int, bool]:
    """Check C(|A|, h) <= h(N-1) + 1 with N = max(A) + 1."""
    n_big = max(a) + 1
    lhs = comb(len(a), h)
    rhs = h * (n_big - 1) + 1
    return lhs, rhs, lhs <= rhs

from typing import List, Set, Tuple


def greedy_difference_sidon(n_terms: int) -> Tuple[List[int], List[int]]:
    """Return the first n_terms of the greedy difference-avoiding set, together
    with the number of candidates rejected before each acceptance.

    Invariant: `realised` holds every difference x - y (x != y) available from
    the current set A.  A candidate m is accepted exactly when the 2|A| new
    differences +-(m - a) are pairwise distinct and disjoint from `realised`.
    Since m differs from every a, the new differences are automatically
    pairwise distinct unless m - a = a' - m for some a, a', i.e. unless
    2m = a + a' -- the halving obstruction.  Both checks are performed.

    Complexity: O(|A|) hash operations per candidate; the n-th element is found
    after O(n^3) candidates by the cubic bound, so O(n^4) overall for n terms.
    """
    a: List[int] = []
    realised: Set[int] = set()
    rejections: List[int] = []
    m, rejected = 0, 0
    while len(a) < n_terms:
        fresh: Set[int] = set()
        ok = True
        for x in a:
            for d in (m - x, x - m):
                if d in realised or d in fresh:
                    ok = False
                    break
                fresh.add(d)
            if not ok:
                break
        if ok:
            a.append(m)
            realised |= fresh
            rejections.append(rejected)
            rejected = 0
        else:
            rejected += 1
        m += 1
    return a, rejections


def greedy_sum_sidon(n_terms: int) -> List[int]:
    """The same object built by avoiding repeated *sums* instead.

    The two constructions coincide, because a - b = c - d is the same
    coincidence as a + d = c + b.
    """
    a: List[int] = []
    sums: Set[int] = set()
    m = 0
    while len(a) < n_terms:
        fresh = {m + x for x in a} | {2 * m}
        if len(fresh) == len(a) + 1 and not (fresh & sums):
            a.append(m)
            sums |= fresh
        m += 1
    return a

from itertools import product
from typing import List, Optional, Set, Tuple


def cubic_obstruction(a: List[int]) -> Set[int]:
    """Bad(A) = {c + d - b : b, c, d in A}; at most |A|^3 integers."""
    return {c + d - b for b, c, d in product(a, repeat=3)}


def halving_obstruction(a: List[int]) -> Set[int]:
    """Half(A) = {m : 2m = c + d}; at most |A|^2 integers."""
    return {(c + d) // 2 for c, d in product(a, repeat=2) if (c + d) % 2 == 0}


def greedy_step(a: List[int]) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
    """Return (m, |Bad(A)|, |Half(A)|) where m is the least admissible value.

    Correctness: for m not in A, A + {m} is a Sidon set precisely when A is a
    Sidon set, m avoids Bad(A) and m avoids Half(A).  Termination: the
    forbidden values number at most |A|^3 + |A|^2 + |A|, so a survivor exists in
    {0, 1, ..., |A|^3 + |A|^2 + |A|}.  Chain rigidity guarantees the survivor
    found by the greedy chain is above every earlier element, so no ordering
    test is needed.

    Complexity: O(|A|^3) time and space to build the obstruction sets, then
    O(|A|^3) scan.
    """
    n = len(a)
    bad, half, present = cubic_obstruction(a), halving_obstruction(a), set(a)
    for m in range(n**3 + n**2 + n + 1):
        if m not in present and m not in bad and m not in half:
            return m, len(bad), len(half)
    raise RuntimeError("pigeonhole failed — impossible by the cubic bound")


def build(n_terms: int) -> List[int]:
    a: List[int] = []
    while len(a) < n_terms:
        m, _, _ = greedy_step(a)
        a.append(m)
    return a

    """Return None if A + {m} is Sidon, else a human-readable violation."""
    if m in a:

    if m in cubic_obstruction(a):

            if 2 * m == c + d:

    return None

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import combinations_with_replacement
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

Multiset = Tuple[int, ...]
Formal = Tuple[Tuple[int, int], ...]


def formal_difference(s: Multiset, t: Multiset) -> Formal:
    """Canonical form of s - t in the free abelian group on the ground set."""
    counts: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for x in s:
        counts[x] = counts.get(x, 0) + 1
    for x in t:
        counts[x] = counts.get(x, 0) - 1
    return tuple(sorted((x, c) for x, c in counts.items() if c != 0))


def is_diff_bh(a: List[int], h: int) -> bool:
    """Decide h-fold difference rigidity.

    The conclusion s + t' = s' + t is exactly equality of the formal differences
    s - t and s' - t', so rigidity says: the numeric value sum(s) - sum(t)
    determines the formal difference.  One hash table therefore decides it.

    Complexity: M^2 formal differences with M = C(|A| + h - 1, h), each built in
    O(h); i.e. O(M^2 h) time and O(M^2) space in the worst case.
    """
    ms: List[Multiset] = list(combinations_with_replacement(sorted(a), h))
    seen: Dict[int, Formal] = {}
    for s in ms:
        ssum = sum(s)
        for t in ms:
            key = ssum - sum(t)
            f = formal_difference(s, t)
            if key in seen and seen[key] != f:
                return False
            seen[key] = f
    return True


def bh_witness(a: List[int], h: int) -> Optional[Tuple[Multiset, Multiset]]:
    """A pair of distinct size-h multisets of A with equal sums, if any."""
    seen: Dict[int, Multiset] = {}
    for s in combinations_with_replacement(sorted(a), h):
        total = sum(s)
        if total in seen and seen[total] != s:
            return seen[total], s
        seen[total] = s
    return None


def is_bh(a: List[int], h: int) -> bool:
    return bh_witness(a, h) is None


def audit_collapse(sets: List[List[int]], max_h: int = 3) -> bool:
    """Verify Diff_h <=> B_{2h} on a family of sets; return True if it holds."""
    for a in sets:
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1):
            if is_diff_bh(a, h) != is_bh(a, 2 * h):
                print(f"MISMATCH: A = {a}, h = {h}")
                return False
    return True

    for i in range(len(a)):

*A guided tour of non-repetitive sets: rulers whose distances never repeat, the greedy algorithm
that builds them, and the surprise that appears when pairs are replaced by $h$-tuples.*

---

## 0 · The question in one picture

Put a handful of marks on a ruler. Measure every distance between two marks. If no distance is ever
measured twice, the ruler is called a **perfect difference set** — or, in the language we will use
throughout, a **Sidon set**. Such rulers are the combinatorial backbone of
[sparse antenna arrays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparse_array),
[Golomb rulers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golomb_ruler), sonar patterns and optical orthogonal
codes: distinct distances mean unambiguous measurements.

The simplest way to build one is to be greedy. Start empty; repeatedly add the smallest number that
does not repeat a distance. Play with the result before we prove anything about it.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

Three things in that laboratory are worth noticing, and each is a theorem.

1. **Sums and differences are the same condition.** Panel 4 tests your set two ways — all pairwise
   sums distinct, and all pairwise differences distinct — and the two verdicts never disagree.
2. **The forbidden set is cubic and explicitly describable.** Panel 2 draws it.
3. **The growth is trapped between $n^2/2$ and $n^3$.** Panel 3 draws that too.

---

## 1 · Why sums and differences are the same condition

> **Definition.** A finite set $A$ of non-negative integers is a **Sidon set** if
> $a + b = c + d$ with $a,b,c,d \in A$ forces $\{a,b\} = \{c,d\}$.

> **Theorem (Sums $\Leftrightarrow$ differences).** $A$ is a Sidon set if and only if the map
> $(a,b) \mapsto a - b$ is injective on pairs of *distinct* elements of $A$.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proof</b> (three lines of arithmetic)</summary>

If $a - b = c - d$ with $a \ne b$ and $c \ne d$, then $a + d = c + b$. The Sidon dichotomy gives
either $(a = c,\ d = b)$ — which is the injectivity conclusion — or $(a = b,\ d = c)$, which
contradicts $a \ne b$.

Conversely, suppose $a + b = c + d$. If $a = c$ then $b = d$. Otherwise $a \ne c$, and the equation
forces $d \ne b$, so $(a,c)$ and $(d,b)$ are off-diagonal pairs with $a - c = d - b$; injectivity
gives $a = d$ and $c = b$. $\blacksquare$

The subtle point is that this is a statement about $\mathbb{N}$, which is **not** a group. The
differences have to be taken in $\mathbb{Z}$, but the Sidon condition never leaves $\mathbb{N}$.
</details>

The consequence is immediate and slightly deflating: the two greedy algorithms you might write —
avoid a repeated sum, avoid a repeated difference — are one algorithm. Here it is, in both guises.

{{algorithm:0}}

Its output begins $0, 1, 3, 7, 12, 20, 30, 44, 65, 80, \dots$, which is the classical
[Mian–Chowla sequence](https://oeis.org/A005282) shifted by one.

---

## 2 · The obstruction: a cubic cloud

Why does the greedy step never get stuck? Because failure has a completely explicit description.

> **Theorem (Exact greedy step).** Let $A$ be a Sidon set and let $m$ exceed every element of $A$.
> Then $A \cup \{m\}$ is a Sidon set **if and only if**
> $$m \notin \mathrm{Bad}(A) := \{\,c + d - b \ :\ b, c, d \in A\,\},$$
> a set of at most $|A|^3$ integers.

The equation $m = c + d - b$ is just $m - c = d - b$ rearranged: it says the new mark repeats an old
distance. Among any $|A|^3 + 1$ consecutive integers, one escapes the cloud, so a legal step always
exists.

<details>
<summary><b>The second obstruction — what happens if the candidate is allowed to sit low</b></summary>

Drop the requirement $m > \max A$ and a new failure mode appears: $m + m = c + d$, i.e. $m$ is the
midpoint of two elements. This **halving obstruction** is much smaller — at most $|A|^2$ values —
but it is genuinely necessary. The smallest witness is $A = \{0,2\}$ with $m = 1$: the candidate
avoids the cubic cloud completely, yet $\{0,1,2\}$ is not Sidon because $0 + 2 = 1 + 1$. And it is
not a small-set accident: doubling *any* greedy Sidon set of size $k$ and offering $m = 1$ produces
a witness of every size $k \ge 2$.

With both obstructions in hand, the criterion becomes an exact biconditional for candidates
anywhere: for $m \notin A$, the set $A \cup \{m\}$ is Sidon iff $A$ is Sidon and $m$ avoids both
clouds.
</details>

{{algorithm:1}}

## 3 · Greed is rigid, and rigidity is worth a full degree

Here is the structural observation that makes everything sharp.

> **Theorem (Chain rigidity).** If $m$ is not among the first $n$ greedy marks and adding $m$ to them
> still yields a Sidon set, then $m$ is larger than *every* one of those marks.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proof</b> (induction, two sentences)</summary>

Suppose $m \notin G_{n+1}$ and $G_{n+1} \cup \{m\}$ is Sidon. Subsets of Sidon sets are Sidon, so
$G_n \cup \{m\}$ is Sidon, and by induction $m$ exceeds everything in $G_n$. Hence $m$ was a
competitor in the minimisation that produced the $n$-th mark $a(n)$, so $a(n) \le m$; since
$m \ne a(n)$ we get $a(n) < m$, and $m$ exceeds everything in $G_{n+1}$. $\blacksquare$

Note what the argument uses: only that the property is inherited by subsets, and that each greedy
choice was a minimum. It is a general fact about greedy chains, not a fact about Sidon sets.
</details>

Rigidity means the greedy value can be located by a *single* pigeonhole over an interval instead of
by adding one search window per stage. The saving is exactly one degree:

$$\underbrace{4\,a(n) \le (n+1)^4}_{\text{window summation}} \qquad\longrightarrow\qquad
\underbrace{a(n) \le n^3 + n^2 + n}_{\text{one global pigeonhole}}.$$

From below, counting distances gives $n(n+1) \le 2\,a(n)$: a set of $n+1$ marks inside
$\{0,\dots,a(n)\}$ realises $(n+1)n$ distinct non-zero differences, all inside an interval holding
only $2a(n)$ of them. Verify the whole picture numerically:

## 4 · From pairs to $h$-tuples: the $B_h$ tower

> **Definition.** $A$ is a **$B_h$ set** if a multiset of $h$ elements of $A$ is determined by its
> sum: whenever $s$ and $t$ are $h$-element multisets over $A$ with $\sum s = \sum t$, we have
> $s = t$.

$B_1$ is no condition; $B_2$ is exactly Sidon; higher $h$ is harsher. The floors nest,
$$\cdots \subseteq B_4 \subseteq B_3 \subseteq B_2 \subseteq B_1,$$
by a padding argument, and the nesting is strict at every level.

Now, Sidon-ness had a difference formulation, so the higher floors should too:

> **Definition.** $A$ has **$h$-fold difference rigidity**, written $\mathrm{Diff}_h$, if for all
> $h$-element multisets $s, t, s', t'$ over $A$,
> $$\textstyle \sum s - \sum t = \sum s' - \sum t' \ \Longrightarrow\ s + t' = s' + t.$$
> (The additive form of the conclusion is what makes the definition meaningful over $\mathbb{N}$,
> where subtraction is truncated; over a group it says $s - t = s' - t'$.)

At $h = 1$ this is literally "all differences are distinct", so $\mathrm{Diff}_1$ is the Sidon
condition. Two implications are easy — and they suggest a new layer wedged between two old ones:
$$B_{2h} \ \Longrightarrow\ \mathrm{Diff}_h \ \Longrightarrow\ B_h.$$

Explore both towers, and try to find a set where the middle layer differs from $B_{2h}$:

{{interactive_demo:1}}

---

## 5 · The collapse

You will not find one.

> **Theorem (Collapse).** $\mathrm{Diff}_h$ is *equivalent* to $B_{2h}$.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proof</b> (the missing implication is one idea)</summary>

$B_{2h} \Rightarrow \mathrm{Diff}_h$: given the hypothesis, $s + t'$ and $s' + t$ are two multisets
of $2h$ elements with the same sum, so $B_{2h}$ makes them equal.

$\mathrm{Diff}_h \Rightarrow B_{2h}$: let $u, v$ be $2h$-element multisets over $A$ with
$\sum u = \sum v$. **Cut each in half**: write $u = s + t'$ and $v = s' + t$ with all four pieces of
size $h$. The equality $\sum u = \sum v$ is *literally* the hypothesis of rigidity, so rigidity
returns $s + t' = s' + t$, i.e. $u = v$. $\blacksquare$

The remaining implication $\mathrm{Diff}_h \Rightarrow B_h$ (the weak half of the sandwich) comes
from the degenerate difference $\sum s - \sum t = \sum t - \sum s$, which yields $s + s = t + t$ and
hence $s = t$.
</details>

So the difference hierarchy is the **even part** of the sum hierarchy — no new floors. Two morals:

- **Explanatory.** At $h = 1$, $\mathrm{Diff}_1 = B_2$. That is exactly why greedy difference
  avoidance produces Sidon sets: not a coincidence of small parameters, but an identity of
  conditions.
- **Algorithmic.** To build a $B_{2h}$ set greedily, test for repeated $h$-fold *differences* rather
  than repeated $2h$-fold sums — logically the same test, but on a strictly smaller family of
  coincidences.

Here is the decision procedure that panel 3 of the widget runs, together with an exhaustive audit of
the collapse:

{{algorithm:2}}

<details>
<summary><b>Is the tower real? Three points settle it, at every level</b></summary>

> **Theorem (Strictness).** For every $h \ge 1$, the set $T_h = \{0,\ 1,\ h+1\}$ is a $B_h$ set and
> is not a $B_{h+1}$ set.

The failure at level $h+1$ is the single carry relation
$$\underbrace{1 + 1 + \cdots + 1}_{h+1} \;=\; (h+1) + \underbrace{0 + \cdots + 0}_{h},$$
and the positive half is a one-digit place-value argument: a multiset over $\{0, 1, N\}$ with
$N = h+1$ has sum $c_1 + N c_N$; with only $h$ entries, $c_1 \le h < N$, so $c_1$ is a legitimate
base-$N$ digit and digits are unique. Uniqueness dies exactly when carrying starts, i.e. at
multiplicity $h+1$.

Since $\mathrm{Diff}_h = B_{2h}$, the same three-point family separates the difference layers too.
For $h = 2$: the greedy set $\{0,1,3\}$ is Sidon but not $B_3$, because $0 + 0 + 3 = 1 + 1 + 1$.
</details>

---

## 6 · Greed at every floor

The whole machine lifts. For $B_h$, a candidate $m$ fails exactly through a **weighted, signed**
equation: after cancelling the copies of $m$ common to both sides,
$$d\,m + \Sigma_0 = \Sigma_1, \qquad 1 \le d \le h,$$
where $\Sigma_0, \Sigma_1$ are sums of at most $h$ elements of $A$. Since $m$ is determined by
$(d, \Sigma_1, \Sigma_0)$, the bad set is finite: at most $h\big((h+1)(|A|+1)^h\big)^2$ values.
Chain rigidity transports verbatim, and one pigeonhole gives
$$a_h(n) \le n + h\big((h+1)(n+1)^h\big)^2 \qquad (\text{degree } 2h),$$
while the counting bound for $B_h$ sets — distinct $h$-element subsets have distinct sums, and all
those sums fit in $\{0, \dots, h(N-1)\}$, so $\binom{|A|}{h} \le h(N-1) + 1$ — gives
$$\binom{n+1}{h} \le h\,a_h(n) + 1 \qquad (\text{degree } h).$$

The single weight $d$ is where all the extra difficulty of the higher floors lives: for Sidon sets
$d \in \{1,2\}$, and $d = 2$ is precisely the halving obstruction.

{{visualization:0}}

<details>
<summary><b>How wide is the remaining gap, really?</b></summary>

For $h = 2$ the proved sandwich is $n^2/2 \le a(n) \le n^3+n^2+n$, and the data ($a(13) = 181$ against
$91$ and $2379$) suggest the cubic side is closer to the truth. Improving it is *not* a matter of
counting the obstruction better — it really does have about $n^3$ points — but of showing those
points are **dispersed** over an interval of length $\asymp \max A$ rather than clustered.

For general $h$ the situation reverses: the degree-$h$ counting bound is the sharp side, and the
degree-$2h$ pigeonhole is far off. The greedy $B_3$ and $B_4$ sequences
$0, 1, 4, 13, 32, 71, 124, 218, 375$ and $0, 1, 5, 21, 55, 153, 368, 856$ (the classical
[$B_3$](https://oeis.org/A046185) and [$B_4$](https://oeis.org/A046186) listings, shifted by one)
look like degree $2h - 1$.
</details>

## 8 · What to take away

1. **A signed condition is an unsigned condition with terms moved across the equals sign.** That is
   why the difference tower is the even part of the sum tower, and why the only invariant that
   survives is the total positive mass. It also suggests the right conjecture for general integer
   weights $\sum_i w_i x_i$.
2. **Greedy chains remember their past.** The fact that nothing was skipped earlier is a global
   constraint on what can happen later. Cashing it in replaced a sum of windows by one pigeonhole
   and saved a full degree, at every floor of the tower. Nothing in that argument is specific to
   non-repetitive sets: it works for any property inherited by subsets.
3. **Hierarchies collapse more often than we expect.** The productive move is to try to separate two
   adjacent floors — and to read the failure carefully when the attempt does not work.

/-! ## 1. Sumsets of bounded length -/

/-- The `k`-fold sumset of `A` (with repetition allowed). -/
def sumPow (A : Finset ℕ) : ℕ → Finset ℕ
  | 0 => {0}
  | k + 1 => sumPow A k + A

theorem card_sumPow_le (A : Finset ℕ) : ∀ k, #(sumPow A k) ≤ #A ^ k
  | 0 => by simp [sumPow]
  | k + 1 => by
      calc #(sumPow A (k + 1)) ≤ #(sumPow A k) * #A := Finset.card_add_le
        _ ≤ #A ^ k * #A := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (card_sumPow_le A k)
        _ = #A ^ (k + 1) := by ring

/-- Every multiset of `k` elements of `A` has its sum in the `k`-fold sumset. -/
theorem sum_mem_sumPow {A : Finset ℕ} (k : ℕ) : ∀ s : Multiset ℕ, (∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ A) →
    Multiset.card s = k → s.sum ∈ sumPow A k := by
  induction k with
  | zero =>
      intro s _ hcs
      rw [Multiset.card_eq_zero.mp hcs]
      simp [sumPow]
  | succ k ih =>
      intro s hs hcs
      have hpos : 0 < Multiset.card s := by omega
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := Multiset.card_pos_iff_exists_mem.mp hpos
      obtain ⟨s', rfl⟩ := Multiset.exists_cons_of_mem ha
      have hcs' : Multiset.card s' = k := by
        rw [Multiset.card_cons] at hcs; omega
      have hs' : ∀ x ∈ s', x ∈ A := fun x hx => hs x (Multiset.mem_cons_of_mem hx)
      have haA : a ∈ A := hs a (Multiset.mem_cons_self _ _)
      have hmem := ih s' hs' hcs'
      rw [Multiset.sum_cons, Nat.add_comm a s'.sum]
      exact Finset.add_mem_add hmem haA

/-- The sums of at most `h` elements of `A`. -/
def sumsUpTo (A : Finset ℕ) (h : ℕ) : Finset ℕ := (Finset.range (h + 1)).biUnion (sumPow A)

theorem sum_mem_sumsUpTo {A : Finset ℕ} {h : ℕ} {s : Multiset ℕ} (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ A)
    (hcs : Multiset.card s ≤ h) : s.sum ∈ sumsUpTo A h := by
  refine Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨Multiset.card s, ?_, sum_mem_sumPow _ s hs rfl⟩
  rw [Finset.mem_range]; omega

theorem card_sumsUpTo_le (A : Finset ℕ) (h : ℕ) : #(sumsUpTo A h) ≤ (h + 1) * (#A + 1) ^ h := by
  calc #(sumsUpTo A h) ≤ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (h + 1), #(sumPow A k) :=

    _ ≤ ∑ _k ∈ Finset.range (h + 1), (#A + 1) ^ h := by

        calc #(sumPow A k) ≤ #A ^ k := card_sumPow_le A k
          _ ≤ (#A + 1) ^ k := Nat.pow_le_pow_left (by omega) k
          _ ≤ (#A + 1) ^ h := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
    _ = (h + 1) * (#A + 1) ^ h := by
        rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_range, smul_eq_mul]

/-! ## 2. The weighted obstruction set -/

/-- The **weighted obstruction set** for a greedy `B_h` step: the candidates `m` solving
`d · m + y = x` for some weight `1 ≤ d ≤ h` and sums `x, y` of at most `h` elements of
`A`. -/
def bhBad (A : Finset ℕ) (h : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  ((Finset.Icc 1 h) ×ˢ (sumsUpTo A h) ×ˢ (sumsUpTo A h)).image fun p => (p.2.1 - p.2.2) / p.1

theorem card_bhBad_le (A : Finset ℕ) (h : ℕ) : #(bhBad A h) ≤ h * #(sumsUpTo A h) ^ 2 := by
  refine le_trans Finset.card_image_le ?_
  rw [Finset.card_product, Finset.card_product, Nat.card_Icc, pow_two]
  have hh : h + 1 - 1 = h := by omega
  rw [hh]

theorem mem_bhBad_of {A : Finset ℕ} {h d m x y : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdh : d ≤ h)
    (hx : x ∈ sumsUpTo A h) (hy : y ∈ sumsUpTo A h) (heq : d * m + y = x) :
    m ∈ bhBad A h := by
  refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(d, x, y), ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_Icc, hd, hdh, hx, hy]
  · have : x - y = d * m := by omega
    simp only [this]
    exact Nat.mul_div_cancel_left m hd

/-! ## 3. The greedy step for `B_h` -/

/-- Split a multiset over `insert m A` into its `m`-part and its `A`-part. -/
theorem multiset_split {A : Finset ℕ} {m : ℕ} (s : Multiset ℕ)
    (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ insert m A) :
    s = Multiset.replicate (s.count m) m + s.filter (fun x => ¬ x = m) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ s.filter (fun x => ¬ x = m), x ∈ A) ∧
      Multiset.card (s.filter (fun x => ¬ x = m)) + s.count m = Multiset.card s ∧
      s.sum = s.count m * m + (s.filter (fun x => ¬ x = m)).sum := by
  have hsplit : Multiset.replicate (s.count m) m + s.filter (fun x => ¬ x = m) = s := by
    rw [← Multiset.filter_eq' s m]
    exact Multiset.filter_add_not _ s
  refine ⟨hsplit.symm, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x hx
    have hx1 : x ∈ s := Multiset.mem_of_mem_filter hx
    have hx2 : ¬ x = m := (Multiset.mem_filter.mp hx).2
    rcases Finset.mem_insert.mp (hs x hx1) with h | h
    · exact absurd h hx2
    · exact h
  · have := congrArg Multiset.card hsplit
    rw [Multiset.card_add, Multiset.card_replicate] at this
    omega
  · have := congrArg Multiset.sum hsplit
    rw [Multiset.sum_add, Multiset.sum_replicate, smul_eq_mul] at this
    omega

/-- If the `m`-multiplicities differ, the candidate `m` lies in the obstruction set. -/
theorem mem_bhBad_of_count_lt {A : Finset ℕ} {h m : ℕ} {s t : Multiset ℕ}
    (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ insert m A) (ht : ∀ x ∈ t, x ∈ insert m A)
    (hcs : Multiset.card s = h) (hct : Multiset.card t = h) (hsum : s.sum = t.sum)
    (hlt : t.count m < s.count m) : m ∈ bhBad A h := by
  obtain ⟨-, hs0A, hs0card, hs0sum⟩ := multiset_split s hs
  obtain ⟨-, ht0A, ht0card, ht0sum⟩ := multiset_split t ht
  set j := s.count m
  set k := t.count m
  set s0 := s.filter (fun x => ¬ x = m)
  set t0 := t.filter (fun x => ¬ x = m)
  have hxs : s0.sum ∈ sumsUpTo A h := sum_mem_sumsUpTo hs0A (by omega)
  have hxt : t0.sum ∈ sumsUpTo A h := sum_mem_sumsUpTo ht0A (by omega)
  refine mem_bhBad_of (d := j - k) (by omega) (by omega) hxt hxs ?_
  have hjm : j * m = k * m + (j - k) * m := by
    rw [← Nat.add_mul]
    congr 1
    omega
  have e1 : j * m + s0.sum = k * m + t0.sum := by rw [← hs0sum, ← ht0sum]; exact hsum
  rw [hjm] at e1
  omega

/-- **The greedy step for `B_h`.**  A candidate above `A` avoiding the weighted obstruction
set keeps the `B_h` property. -/
theorem isBh_insert_of_notMem_bhBad {A : Finset ℕ} {h m : ℕ} (hA : IsBh h A)
    (hbad : m ∉ bhBad A h) : IsBh h (insert m A) := by
  intro s t hs ht hcs hct hsum
  obtain ⟨hseq, hs0A, hs0card, hs0sum⟩ := multiset_split s hs
  obtain ⟨hteq, ht0A, ht0card, ht0sum⟩ := multiset_split t ht
  rcases lt_trichotomy (s.count m) (t.count m) with hlt | heq | hgt
  · exact absurd (mem_bhBad_of_count_lt ht hs hct hcs hsum.symm hlt) hbad
  · -- equal multiplicities: reduce to `B_{h - j}` for `A`
    set j := s.count m with hj
    set s0 := s.filter (fun x => ¬ x = m)
    set t0 := t.filter (fun x => ¬ x = m)
    have hcard0 : Multiset.card s0 = h - j := by omega
    have hcard0' : Multiset.card t0 = h - j := by omega
    have hsums : s0.sum = t0.sum := by
      rw [heq] at hs0sum
      omega
    have hs0t0 : s0 = t0 := by
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (h - j) with hz | hpos
      · rw [Multiset.card_eq_zero.mp (by omega : Multiset.card s0 = 0),
          Multiset.card_eq_zero.mp (by omega : Multiset.card t0 = 0)]
      · exact hA.antitone hpos (by omega) s0 t0 hs0A ht0A hcard0 hcard0' hsums
    rw [hseq, hteq, ← heq, hs0t0]
  · exact absurd (mem_bhBad_of_count_lt hs ht hcs hct hsum hgt) hbad

/-- The greedy predicate for `B_h`. -/
def GoodNextBh (h : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ) (m : ℕ) : Prop := (∀ a ∈ A, a < m) ∧ IsBh h (insert m A)

/-- **A greedy `B_h` step always exists**, inside a window of length `h · |S|² + 1`. -/
theorem exists_good_next_bh {A : Finset ℕ} {h : ℕ} (hA : IsBh h A) :
    ∃ m, GoodNextBh h A m ∧ m ≤ A.sup id + h * ((h + 1) * (#A + 1) ^ h) ^ 2 + 1 := by
  classical

  set B := h * ((h + 1) * (#A + 1) ^ h) ^ 2 with hB
  have hbadle : #(bhBad A h) ≤ B := by
    refine le_trans (card_bhBad_le A h) ?_
    rw [hB]
    exact Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (card_sumsUpTo_le A h) 2)
  set S : Finset ℕ := Finset.Icc (M + 1) (M + B + 1) with hS
  have hcardS : #S = B + 1 := by rw [hS, Nat.card_Icc]; omega
  have hex : ∃ m ∈ S, m ∉ bhBad A h := by
    by_contra hcon
    push_neg at hcon
    have hle : #S ≤ #(bhBad A h) := Finset.card_le_card hcon
    omega
  obtain ⟨m, hmS, hmbad⟩ := hex
  have hmS' : M + 1 ≤ m ∧ m ≤ M + B + 1 := by simpa [hS, Finset.mem_Icc] using hmS
  have hlt : ∀ a ∈ A, a < m := by
    intro a ha
    have : a ≤ M := Finset.le_sup (f := id) ha
    omega
  exact ⟨m, ⟨hlt, isBh_insert_of_notMem_bhBad hA hmbad⟩, by omega⟩

/-- The least valid greedy `B_h` continuation of `A`. -/
noncomputable def nextGreedyBh (h : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ) : ℕ := sInf {m | GoodNextBh h A m}

theorem goodNextBh_nextGreedyBh {A : Finset ℕ} {h : ℕ} (hA : IsBh h A) :
    GoodNextBh h A (nextGreedyBh h A) := by
  obtain ⟨m, hm, -⟩ := exists_good_next_bh hA
  exact Nat.sInf_mem (s := {m | GoodNextBh h A m}) ⟨m, hm⟩

theorem nextGreedyBh_le {A : Finset ℕ} {h : ℕ} (hA : IsBh h A) :
    nextGreedyBh h A ≤ A.sup id + h * ((h + 1) * (#A + 1) ^ h) ^ 2 + 1 := by
  obtain ⟨m, hm, hmle⟩ := exists_good_next_bh hA
  exact le_trans (Nat.sInf_le (s := {m | GoodNextBh h A m}) hm) hmle

/-- The greedy `B_h` set after `n` steps. -/
noncomputable def greedySetBh (h : ℕ) : ℕ → Finset ℕ
  | 0 => ∅
  | n + 1 => insert (nextGreedyBh h (greedySetBh h n)) (greedySetBh h n)

/-- The greedy `B_h` sequence. -/
noncomputable def greedySeqBh (h n : ℕ) : ℕ := nextGreedyBh h (greedySetBh h n)

theorem greedySetBh_succ (h n : ℕ) :
    greedySetBh h (n + 1) = insert (greedySeqBh h n) (greedySetBh h n) := rfl

theorem isBh_empty (h : ℕ) : IsBh h (∅ : Finset ℕ) := by
  intro s t hs ht hcs hct _
  rcases Multiset.empty_or_exists_mem s with rfl | ⟨a, ha⟩
  · rcases Multiset.empty_or_exists_mem t with rfl | ⟨b, hb⟩
    · rfl
    · exact absurd (ht b hb) (Finset.notMem_empty b)
  · exact absurd (hs a ha) (Finset.notMem_empty a)

theorem greedySetBh_isBh (h : ℕ) : ∀ n, IsBh h (greedySetBh h n)
  | 0 => isBh_empty h
  | n + 1 => (goodNextBh_nextGreedyBh (greedySetBh_isBh h n)).2

theorem lt_greedySeqBh {h n : ℕ} {a : ℕ} (ha : a ∈ greedySetBh h n) : a < greedySeqBh h n :=
  (goodNextBh_nextGreedyBh (greedySetBh_isBh h n)).1 a ha

theorem card_greedySetBh (h : ℕ) : ∀ n, #(greedySetBh h n) = n
  | 0 => rfl
  | n + 1 => by
      have hnot : greedySeqBh h n ∉ greedySetBh h n := fun hmem =>

  refine strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ fun n => ?_

/-- The greedy window width at stage `n`. -/
def windowBh (h n : ℕ) : ℕ := h * ((h + 1) * (n + 1) ^ h) ^ 2 + 1

theorem windowBh_mono (h : ℕ) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) : windowBh h m ≤ windowBh h n := by
  have h1 : (m + 1) ^ h ≤ (n + 1) ^ h := Nat.pow_le_pow_left (by omega) h
  have h2 : (h + 1) * (m + 1) ^ h ≤ (h + 1) * (n + 1) ^ h := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ h1
  have h3 : ((h + 1) * (m + 1) ^ h) ^ 2 ≤ ((h + 1) * (n + 1) ^ h) ^ 2 :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_left h2 2
  unfold windowBh
  exact Nat.add_le_add_right (Nat.mul_le_mul_left h h3) 1

  have hb := nextGreedyBh_le (greedySetBh_isBh h (n + 1))

  simpa [windowBh, greedySeqBh, Nat.add_assoc] using hb

namespace GreedyDifference

open Finset

/-! ## 1. Sums versus differences over `ℕ` -/

/-- **Sums ⟺ differences.**  A finite set of naturals is a Sidon set exactly when its
integer differences `a - b` (`a ≠ b`) are pairwise distinct.  Over a group this is
`IsSidon.sub_injOn` plus its converse; `ℕ` is not a group, so the differences must be
taken in `ℤ`. -/
theorem isSidon_iff_sub_injOn (A : Finset ℕ) :
    IsSidon A ↔ Set.InjOn (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => (p.1 : ℤ) - (p.2 : ℤ)) (A.offDiag : Set (ℕ × ℕ)) := by
  constructor
  · rintro hA ⟨a, b⟩ hp ⟨c, d⟩ hq h
    simp only [Finset.coe_offDiag, Set.mem_offDiag] at hp hq
    obtain ⟨ha, hb, hab⟩ := hp
    obtain ⟨hc, hd, -⟩ := hq
    simp only at h
    have h' : a + d = c + b := by omega
    rcases hA a ha d hd c hc b hb h' with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, -⟩
    · simp [h1, h2]
    · exact absurd h1 hab
  · intro hinj a ha b hb c hc d hd habcd
    by_cases hac : a = c
    · exact Or.inl ⟨hac, by omega⟩
    · have hdb : d ≠ b := by omega
      have h1 : ((a, c) : ℕ × ℕ) ∈ (A.offDiag : Set (ℕ × ℕ)) := by
        simp [Finset.coe_offDiag, Set.mem_offDiag, ha, hc, hac]
      have h2 : ((d, b) : ℕ × ℕ) ∈ (A.offDiag : Set (ℕ × ℕ)) := by
        simp [Finset.coe_offDiag, Set.mem_offDiag, hd, hb, hdb]
      have heq := hinj h1 h2 (by simp only; omega)
      have h3 : a = d := (Prod.ext_iff.mp heq).1
      have h4 : c = b := (Prod.ext_iff.mp heq).2
      exact Or.inr ⟨h3, h4.symm⟩

/-! ## 2. The difference-obstruction set -/

/-- The **difference obstruction set** of a finite `A ⊆ ℕ`: the integers `c + d - b`
with `b, c, d ∈ A`.  A candidate `m` above `A` may be adjoined to `A` without repeating
a difference precisely when `(m : ℤ)` avoids this set. -/
def sidonBad (A : Finset ℕ) : Finset ℤ :=
  (A ×ˢ A ×ˢ A).image fun p => (p.2.1 : ℤ) + (p.2.2 : ℤ) - (p.1 : ℤ)

theorem mem_sidonBad_of_eq {A : Finset ℕ} {m b c d : ℕ} (hb : b ∈ A) (hc : c ∈ A) (hd : d ∈ A)
    (h : m + b = c + d) : (m : ℤ) ∈ sidonBad A := by
  refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(b, c, d), ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [Finset.mem_product, hb, hc, hd]
  · have : (m : ℤ) + b = (c : ℤ) + d := by exact_mod_cast congrArg (Nat.cast : ℕ → ℤ) h
    simp only
    omega

theorem exists_of_mem_sidonBad {A : Finset ℕ} {m : ℕ} (h : (m : ℤ) ∈ sidonBad A) :
    ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, ∃ d ∈ A, m + b = c + d := by
  obtain ⟨⟨b, c, d⟩, hmem, heq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp h
  simp only [Finset.mem_product] at hmem
  refine ⟨b, hmem.1, c, hmem.2.1, d, hmem.2.2, ?_⟩
  have : (m : ℤ) + b = (c : ℤ) + d := by simp only at heq; omega
  exact_mod_cast this

/-- **The obstruction set is exactly the set of difference repetitions.**  `m` is
forbidden iff adjoining it would create a difference `m - c` already present as `d - b`
inside `A`. -/
theorem mem_sidonBad_iff_repeats_difference (A : Finset ℕ) (m : ℕ) :
    (m : ℤ) ∈ sidonBad A ↔
      ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, ∃ d ∈ A, (m : ℤ) - (c : ℤ) = (d : ℤ) - (b : ℤ) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨b, hb, c, hc, d, hd, heq⟩ := exists_of_mem_sidonBad h
    exact ⟨b, hb, c, hc, d, hd, by exact_mod_cast (by omega : (m : ℤ) - c = (d : ℤ) - b)⟩
  · rintro ⟨b, hb, c, hc, d, hd, heq⟩
    refine mem_sidonBad_of_eq hb hc hd ?_
    have : (m : ℤ) + b = (c : ℤ) + d := by omega
    exact_mod_cast this

/-- The obstruction set has at most `|A|³` elements. -/
theorem card_sidonBad_le (A : Finset ℕ) : #(sidonBad A) ≤ #A ^ 3 := by
  refine le_trans (Finset.card_image_le) ?_
  rw [Finset.card_product, Finset.card_product]
  ring_nf
  omega

/-! ## 3. The exact greedy step criterion -/

/-- **Greedy step criterion.**  For a candidate `m` strictly larger than every element of
`A`, the enlarged set `insert m A` is Sidon iff `A` is Sidon and `m` avoids the
difference obstruction set.  (Both implications hold: the obstruction set is exactly
right, not merely sufficient.) -/
theorem isSidon_insert_iff {A : Finset ℕ} {m : ℕ} (hm : ∀ a ∈ A, a < m) :
    IsSidon (insert m A) ↔ IsSidon A ∧ (m : ℤ) ∉ sidonBad A := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨h.mono (Finset.subset_insert _ _), fun hbad => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨b, hb, c, hc, d, hd, heq⟩ := exists_of_mem_sidonBad hbad
    have hmi : m ∈ insert m A := Finset.mem_insert_self _ _
    have hbi : b ∈ insert m A := Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hb
    have hci : c ∈ insert m A := Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hc
    have hdi : d ∈ insert m A := Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hd
    rcases h m hmi b hbi c hci d hdi heq with ⟨h1, -⟩ | ⟨h1, -⟩
    · exact absurd (h1 ▸ hm c hc) (lt_irrefl m)
    · exact absurd (h1 ▸ hm d hd) (lt_irrefl m)
  · rintro ⟨hA, hbad⟩ a ha b hb c hc d hd habcd
    -- decompose membership in `insert m A`
    have key : ∀ x ∈ insert m A, x = m ∨ (x ∈ A ∧ x < m) := by
      intro x hx
      rcases Finset.mem_insert.mp hx with h | h
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨h, hm x h⟩
    have hbadn : ∀ b' ∈ A, ∀ c' ∈ A, ∀ d' ∈ A, m + b' ≠ c' + d' := by
      intro b' hb' c' hc' d' hd' heq
      exact hbad (mem_sidonBad_of_eq hb' hc' hd' heq)
    rcases key a ha with ha' | ⟨haA, halt⟩ <;> rcases key b hb with hb' | ⟨hbA, hblt⟩ <;>
      rcases key c hc with hc' | ⟨hcA, hclt⟩ <;> rcases key d hd with hd' | ⟨hdA, hdlt⟩ <;>
      first
        | omega
        | exact absurd (show m + b = c + d by omega) (hbadn b hbA c hcA d hdA)
        | exact absurd (show m + a = c + d by omega) (hbadn a haA c hcA d hdA)
        | exact absurd (show m + d = a + b by omega) (hbadn d hdA a haA b hbA)
        | exact absurd (show m + c = a + b by omega) (hbadn c hcA a haA b hbA)
        | exact hA a haA b hbA c hcA d hdA habcd

/-! ## 4. Existence of a greedy step -/

/-- The greedy predicate: `m` sits strictly above `A` and keeps the set Sidon. -/
def GoodNext (A : Finset ℕ) (m : ℕ) : Prop := (∀ a ∈ A, a < m) ∧ IsSidon (insert m A)

instance (A : Finset ℕ) : DecidablePred (GoodNext A) := fun _ => by
  unfold GoodNext; infer_instance

/-- **A greedy step always exists, inside a cubic window.**  If `A` is Sidon then some
`m` in the interval `(max A, max A + |A|³ + 1]` extends it. -/
theorem exists_good_next {A : Finset ℕ} (hA : IsSidon A) :
    ∃ m, GoodNext A m ∧ m ≤ A.sup id + #A ^ 3 + 1 := by
  classical
  set M := A.sup id with hM
  set S : Finset ℕ := Finset.Icc (M + 1) (M + #A ^ 3 + 1) with hS
  have hcardS : #S = #A ^ 3 + 1 := by
    rw [hS, Nat.card_Icc]; omega
  have : ∃ m ∈ S, (m : ℤ) ∉ sidonBad A := by
    by_contra hcon
    push_neg at hcon
    have hinj : Set.InjOn (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℤ)) (S : Set ℕ) := fun x _ y _ h =>
      Nat.cast_injective h
    have hle : #S ≤ #(sidonBad A) :=
      Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn _ (fun x hx => hcon x hx) hinj
    have := card_sidonBad_le A
    omega
  obtain ⟨m, hmS, hmbad⟩ := this
  have hmS' : M + 1 ≤ m ∧ m ≤ M + #A ^ 3 + 1 := by
    simpa [hS, Finset.mem_Icc] using hmS
  refine ⟨m, ⟨?_, ?_⟩, by omega⟩
  · intro a ha
    have : a ≤ M := Finset.le_sup (f := id) ha
    omega
  · exact (isSidon_insert_iff (fun a ha => by
      have : a ≤ M := Finset.le_sup (f := id) ha
      omega)).mpr ⟨hA, hmbad⟩

/-! ## 5. The greedy sequence -/

/-- The least valid greedy continuation of `A` (junk value `0` if none exists, which by
`exists_good_next` happens only for non-Sidon `A`). -/
noncomputable def nextGreedy (A : Finset ℕ) : ℕ := sInf {m | GoodNext A m}

theorem goodNext_nextGreedy {A : Finset ℕ} (hA : IsSidon A) : GoodNext A (nextGreedy A) := by
  obtain ⟨m, hm, -⟩ := exists_good_next hA
  exact Nat.sInf_mem (s := {m | GoodNext A m}) ⟨m, hm⟩

theorem nextGreedy_le {A : Finset ℕ} (hA : IsSidon A) :
    nextGreedy A ≤ A.sup id + #A ^ 3 + 1 := by
  obtain ⟨m, hm, hmle⟩ := exists_good_next hA
  exact le_trans (Nat.sInf_le (s := {m | GoodNext A m}) hm) hmle

theorem nextGreedy_eq_of {A : Finset ℕ} {m : ℕ} (h : GoodNext A m)
    (hmin : ∀ k < m, ¬ GoodNext A k) : nextGreedy A = m := by
  refine le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le (s := {m | GoodNext A m}) h) ?_
  by_contra hlt
  push_neg at hlt
  exact hmin _ hlt (Nat.sInf_mem (s := {m | GoodNext A m}) ⟨m, h⟩)

/-- The greedy difference-avoiding set after `n` steps. -/
noncomputable def greedySet : ℕ → Finset ℕ
  | 0 => ∅
  | n + 1 => insert (nextGreedy (greedySet n)) (greedySet n)

/-- The greedy difference-avoiding sequence: `greedySeq n` is the `(n+1)`-st term. -/
noncomputable def greedySeq (n : ℕ) : ℕ := nextGreedy (greedySet n)

theorem greedySet_succ (n : ℕ) : greedySet (n + 1) = insert (greedySeq n) (greedySet n) := rfl

/-- Every element of the greedy set at stage `n` is smaller than the next term. -/
theorem greedySet_isSidon : ∀ n, IsSidon (greedySet n)
  | 0 => isSidon_empty
  | n + 1 => (goodNext_nextGreedy (greedySet_isSidon n)).2

theorem lt_greedySeq {n : ℕ} {a : ℕ} (ha : a ∈ greedySet n) : a < greedySeq n :=
  (goodNext_nextGreedy (greedySet_isSidon n)).1 a ha

theorem card_greedySet : ∀ n, #(greedySet n) = n
  | 0 => rfl
  | n + 1 => by
      have hnot : greedySeq n ∉ greedySet n := fun h => lt_irrefl _ (lt_greedySeq h)
      rw [greedySet_succ, Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hnot, card_greedySet n]

theorem sup_greedySet_succ (n : ℕ) : (greedySet (n + 1)).sup id = greedySeq n := by
  rw [greedySet_succ, Finset.sup_insert]
  have : (greedySet n).sup id ≤ greedySeq n := by
    refine Finset.sup_le fun a ha => le_of_lt (lt_greedySeq ha)
  simpa [id] using max_eq_left this

theorem greedySeq_strictMono : StrictMono greedySeq := by
  refine strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ fun n => ?_
  exact lt_greedySeq (by rw [greedySet_succ]; exact Finset.mem_insert_self _ _)

/-! ## 6. Concrete values: the Mian–Chowla sequence -/

theorem greedySet_zero : greedySet 0 = ∅ := rfl

theorem greedySeq_zero : greedySeq 0 = 0 := by
  refine nextGreedy_eq_of ⟨by simp [greedySet_zero], ?_⟩ (fun k hk => absurd hk (Nat.not_lt_zero k))
  rw [greedySet_zero]
  decide

theorem greedySet_one : greedySet 1 = {0} := by
  rw [greedySet_succ, greedySeq_zero, greedySet_zero]; rfl

theorem greedySeq_one : greedySeq 1 = 1 := by
  rw [greedySeq, greedySet_one]
  refine nextGreedy_eq_of ⟨by decide, by decide⟩ ?_
  intro k hk hcon
  have h0 : 0 < k := hcon.1 0 (by decide)
  omega

theorem greedySet_two : greedySet 2 = {1, 0} := by
  rw [greedySet_succ, greedySeq_one, greedySet_one]

theorem greedySeq_two : greedySeq 2 = 3 := by
  rw [greedySeq, greedySet_two]
  refine nextGreedy_eq_of ⟨by decide, by decide⟩ ?_
  intro k hk hcon
  have h1 : 1 < k := hcon.1 1 (by decide)
  have h2 := hcon.2
  interval_cases k
  · exact absurd h2 (by decide)

theorem greedySet_three : greedySet 3 = {3, 1, 0} := by
  rw [greedySet_succ, greedySeq_two, greedySet_two]

theorem greedySeq_three : greedySeq 3 = 7 := by
  rw [greedySeq, greedySet_three]
  refine nextGreedy_eq_of ⟨by decide, by decide⟩ ?_
  intro k hk hcon
  have h3 : 3 < k := hcon.1 3 (by decide)
  have h2 := hcon.2
  interval_cases k <;> exact absurd h2 (by decide)

/-! ## 7. The sandwich -/

/-- **Greedy step bound.**  `a (n+1) ≤ a n + (n+1)³ + 1`. -/
theorem greedySeq_succ_le (n : ℕ) : greedySeq (n + 1) ≤ greedySeq n + (n + 1) ^ 3 + 1 := by
  have := nextGreedy_le (greedySet_isSidon (n + 1))
  rwa [sup_greedySet_succ, card_greedySet] at this

/-- **Quartic upper bound.**  `4 · a n ≤ (n+1)⁴`. -/
theorem four_mul_greedySeq_le : ∀ n, 4 * greedySeq n ≤ (n + 1) ^ 4
  | 0 => by simp [greedySeq_zero]
  | n + 1 => by
      have h1 := greedySeq_succ_le n
      have h2 := four_mul_greedySeq_le n
      nlinarith [sq_nonneg (n : ℤ), Nat.zero_le n]

/-- **Quadratic lower bound.**  `n(n+1) ≤ 2 · a n`: the greedy set at stage `n+1` is a
Sidon subset of `{0, …, a n}`, so the catalog's Erdős–Turán counting bound applies. -/
theorem mul_le_two_mul_greedySeq (n : ℕ) : n * (n + 1) ≤ 2 * greedySeq n := by
  have hsub : greedySet (n + 1) ⊆ Finset.range (greedySeq n + 1) := by
    intro a ha
    rw [Finset.mem_range]
    rcases Finset.mem_insert.mp (by rwa [greedySet_succ] at ha) with rfl | h
    · omega
    · have := lt_greedySeq h; omega
  have hcard := (greedySet_isSidon (n + 1)).card_mul_pred_le_of_subset_range hsub
  rw [card_greedySet] at hcard
  simp only [Nat.add_sub_cancel] at hcard
  rw [Nat.mul_comm] at hcard
  omega

/-- **The greedy difference-avoidance sandwich.**  The greedy sequence is squeezed
between a quadratic and a quartic. -/
theorem greedySeq_sandwich (n : ℕ) :
    n * (n + 1) ≤ 2 * greedySeq n ∧ 4 * greedySeq n ≤ (n + 1) ^ 4 :=
  ⟨mul_le_two_mul_greedySeq n, four_mul_greedySeq_le n⟩

`Novelty/BhSetsDifferences.lean` proves that `h`-fold difference rigidity is exactly the
`B_{2h}` condition, and that `B_h` sets are `B_k` for `k ≤ h`.  Both statements would be
vacuous if the tower collapsed.  This file shows it does not: for **every** `h ≥ 1` the
three-element set

  `T h = {0, 1, h + 1} ⊆ ℕ`

is a `B_h` set and is **not** a `B_{h+1}` set — the obstruction being the single
coincidence `(h+1)·1 = 1·(h+1)`, i.e. `h+1` copies of `1` and one copy of `h+1` together
with `h` zeros.  Three points therefore already separate every two consecutive floors of
the tower, and consequently separate `Diff_h` from `Diff_{h+1}` as well.

## Main results

* `triple_sum`, `triple_card`, `triple_ext` — the coordinate calculus for multisets drawn
  from `{0, 1, N}` with `N ≥ 2`: a multiset is determined by its three multiplicities, its
  cardinality is their sum, and its sum is `c₁ + N·c_N`.
* `tripleSet_isBh` — `T h` is a `B_h` set: the multiplicity `c₁` of `1` is at most `h < h+1`,
  so the identity `c₁ + (h+1)·c_{h+1} = c₁' + (h+1)·c_{h+1}'` forces the multiplicities to
  agree, a genuine (if small) `p`-adic style digit argument.
* `tripleSet_not_isBh_succ` — `T h` is not `B_{h+1}`, witnessed explicitly.
* `bh_tower_strict` — hence for every `h ≥ 1` there is a set that is `B_h` but not
  `B_{h+1}`; the antitone chain of `Novelty/BhSetsDifferences.lean` is strictly decreasing.
* `diff_tower_strict` — the same conclusion transported to the difference layers: for every
  `h ≥ 1` there is a set with `h`-fold difference rigidity but not `(h+1)`-fold, i.e.
  avoiding repeated `h`-fold differences is strictly weaker than avoiding repeated
  `(h+1)`-fold differences.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): (S1) The `B_h` tower is strict, and strictness should already be
  visible on sets of *bounded size* — one should not need larger and larger sets to
  separate consecutive floors.  (S2) The separating example should be a "digit" example:
  one large element playing the role of a base.
Experiment (Experimenter): direct search over three-element sets found `{0, 1, h+1}`, and
  the two halves were proved.  The failure at level `h+1` is the single relation
  `1 + 1 + ⋯ + 1 = (h+1)`, so the example is as tight as possible: removing any point makes
  the set `B_k` for all `k` (`{0,1}` and `{0,h+1}` are `B_k` for every `k`).
  The greedy Sidon set `{0,1,3}` of the companion file is the case `h = 2` of this family,
  which is why it is Sidon but not `B₃` — an observation first made numerically.
Analysis (Analyst): the mechanism is base-`(h+1)` digit rigidity, exactly as in the
  Erdős–Turán construction of the catalog, but truncated to one digit.  This suggests the
  general principle that `B_h`-ness of digit constructions is controlled by carrying, and
  carrying begins precisely at multiplicity `h+1`.
Critique (Critic): the theorems are guarded by `1 ≤ h`; for `h = 0` the statement is
  meaningless (`B₀` holds for everything, and `B₁` also holds for everything, so no set
  separates the two).  `tripleSet_not_isBh_succ` is a negative statement proved by an
  explicit witness pair, so it cannot be vacuous; `tripleSet_isBh` is not vacuous because
  `T h` has three distinct elements (`h + 1 ≥ 2`).
Synthesis (PI): three points suffice to separate every two consecutive floors of the tower,
  so all the hierarchy statements of the companion files have content.
-/
